records.title: Marmaray: one railway, several evidence boundaries
records.answer: Marmaray is an operating cross-strait railway extended into a suburban corridor. Opening dates and reported use are established official claims; they do not supply a comparable asset-reliability series.
records.scope: One Halkalı–Gebze railway corridor, including the original cross-strait section and subsequent suburban improvements. Gebze extends into Kocaeli; stations, trainsets and the proposed northern railway are not additional counted projects here.
records.stage: Official records date the original crossing to October 29, 2013 and the suburban improvement's completion to March 13, 2019. Current ministry and parliamentary accounts report use, while future northern relief, design capacity and fare entitlements remain different evidence objects.

identity_decision.rationale: Count the integrated named Marmaray railway corridor once, retaining the original crossing and suburban-extension stages inside that identity. Do not count each station, duplicate the crossing as a separate project, add the proposed northern bypass, or confine the Gebze end to Istanbul municipality.

timeline.event: AYGM dates completion of the original Kazlıçeşme–Ayrılık Çeşmesi crossing.
AYGM dates completion of the Gebze–Halkalı suburban improvement.
The ministry announced preliminary financing for a separate northern railway, with tender preparation continuing.
Cutoff for the cumulative Marmaray use later reported at the parliamentary hearing.
Peak-day passenger use identified in the ministry's October 29 anniversary account.
Parliament published the operator chief's account; the ridership cutoff remained September 30.

sections.heading: A crossing that became a corridor
sections.text: Marmaray joins the European and Asian sides through a railway corridor whose stages need separate dates. AYGM identifies the original Kazlıçeşme–Ayrılık Çeşmesi crossing as completed on October 29, 2013. Its suburban-improvement record extends the railway to Halkalı and Gebze and gives March 13, 2019 as completion. The ministry's anniversary account describes the resulting 76.6-kilometre, 43-station line. This dossier counts the integrated corridor once. It is not the road tunnel discussed separately below, and its Gebze end reaches Kocaeli rather than stopping at Istanbul's municipal boundary.

sections.heading: Track design is not delivered throughput
sections.text: The extension description allocates three tracks to different services: two suburban tracks and one for high-speed trains. That layout explains why a commuter railway also belongs in an account of wider rail connectivity. AYGM's stated 1.7-million-passenger daily capacity is a design figure, not observed daily use. It should not be combined with a peak passenger count to manufacture an utilization rate without matching scope and operating assumptions. Nor does the page's description of planned connections prove that every interchange is currently available. A route inventory and a working timetable answer different questions.

sections.heading: Two cumulative totals, not a growth series
sections.text: The October 29 ministry release rounds thirteen years of use to 1.6 billion passengers and identifies 762,870 on October 6 as a record day. Parliament's November 4 report separately relays the operator chief's 1.636-billion cumulative count through September 30. The later publication therefore has an earlier reporting cutoff; subtracting these differently rounded accounts would be misleading. Neither counts unique people or measures reliable journeys. Conflicting daily-service totals within the anniversary release are omitted, as is its premature first-ten-month figure. Parliamentary reporting of management testimony is not independent verification of the underlying operating dataset.

sections.heading: A proposed relief route stays outside operating results
sections.text: A February 24 ministry announcement concerns a separate northern railway via the Yavuz Sultan Selim Bridge and the two airports. It reports a preliminary financing understanding with six institutions while construction tender preparations continued. Relief for Marmaray passenger and freight traffic is an expected benefit, not demonstrated capacity already released. The proposed route is useful dependency context: a future change could alter which traffic shares the existing crossing. It is not another completed Marmaray segment, a current airport-to-airport service, or a third counted project in this group. Later delivery needs its own dated evidence.

sections.heading: Fare access and physical access are separate
sections.text: The family ministry's disability-card FAQ includes Marmaray among urban services covered by free travel and describes a qualifying companion entitlement. This establishes the published fare-policy category, not the condition of a particular journey. A passenger can have an entitlement while still needing a usable route between street, platform and train. The FAQ supplies no station-level lift uptime or assistance-response series, and this review did not test a card or make an eligibility decision for an individual. Metro İstanbul's separate accessibility description must not be borrowed as a Marmaray equipment inspection.

sections.heading: What would improve this account
sections.text: Editorial evidence test: publish matched-period counts of scheduled and completed trains, delay attribution and station access interruptions, with the corridor and denominator held constant. Keep fares, ridership and reliability in different fields. A new northern-railway contract or opening would warrant a separate dated dependency update, not a retrospective change to the 2013 or 2019 milestones. Comparable recurring observations would make it possible to test whether the network is improving service for passengers; an anniversary total alone cannot answer that question. Preserve the official source conflict rather than silently choosing a convenient daily-service number.

next_artifacts: Comparable scheduled/completed train and delay series for the same corridor and reporting period.
Named-station accessibility availability and incident-resolution records.
Dated northern-railway delivery evidence distinct from preliminary finance and expected relief.

records.title: Eurasia Tunnel: road access, contract and operating claims
records.answer: The Eurasia Tunnel is an operating road crossing with a defined concession and approach roads. Its operator's published traffic and systems descriptions are useful evidence, but not independent safety, fiscal or reliability acceptance.
records.scope: One 14.6-kilometre Kazlıçeşme–Göztepe road project, including the 5.4-kilometre tunnel-and-connections portion and 9.2 kilometres of approaches. Decks, approaches and the separate Marmaray railway do not create additional identities.
records.stage: The operator chronology records completion and first vehicle in 2016; its February 2026 HTML announcement summarizes 2025 traffic. Contract structure, modeled benefits, payment rules and described emergency systems are not interchangeable with audited current outcomes.

identity_decision.rationale: Count the Eurasia road tube crossing with its approaches as one named project. The two road decks and connecting works are components rather than independent projects, and the adjacent Marmaray railway remains a separate transport identity with different users, governance and evidence.

timeline.event: Operator chronology records the award of the project contract.
The chronology records the kickoff ceremony; the implementation contract is listed in the same year.
The chronology lists financial close and the start of the contract period.
Completion, launch and the first vehicle are listed at year precision.
The operator published an HTML summary of its 2025 performance report.

sections.heading: The tunnel is part of a longer road project
sections.text: ATAŞ describes a 14.6-kilometre route between Kazlıçeşme and Göztepe. Its 5.4-kilometre portion combines the twin-deck tunnel and connection tunnels; the remaining 9.2 kilometres are approach improvements. Keeping those components visible avoids describing the entire road as undersea tunnel. The operator's chronology traces a June 2008 award, February 2011 kickoff, 2013 financial close and 2016 completion and first vehicle. Those year-level milestones remain year-level here. This is a road project, not Marmaray, even though both cross the strait and contribute to the same city's transport choices.

sections.heading: Financing and concession duration have their own units
sections.text: The operator's masthead sets out a US$1.245-billion investment, split between US$285 million equity and US$960 million loans. It also separates a 29-year contract period into investment and operating periods: four years seven months and twenty-four years five months. These are published project-structure figures, not a fresh financing announcement or an account of current debt. A concession period is also not a measure of daily service quality. The table does not by itself establish total public fiscal exposure, the value of guarantees actually paid, or the net returns received by investors.

sections.heading: Operating systems are evidence of provision, not measured performance
sections.text: The operation page describes automatic incident detection, cameras, fire systems, drainage, emergency telephones, backup power and communications. It also describes staffed patrol and an emergency plan covering twenty-six scenarios. These details explain how the operator intends to detect and manage disruption inside a constrained road environment. They do not provide an independently measured response-time distribution. The page's rapid-response promise is not adopted as a guarantee, and no live control system was tested. The next useful evidence is a dated incident and closure record linked to these arrangements, not another list of installed equipment.

sections.heading: The 2025 traffic summary needs its denominator
sections.text: A February 1, 2026 announcement reports an average of 77,000 daily vehicle passages in 2025 and says that this exceeded the guarantee level. It also presents nine-year cumulative unit-vehicle passages and an economic-value claim. These are the operator's summary claims: passages are not unique vehicles or people, and claimed economic value is not audited profit. Only the HTML announcement was inspected; the linked performance report and its models were not. Without its definitions and underlying series, this account does not convert the summary into independently accepted congestion, emissions, safety or public-finance outcomes.

sections.heading: Payment design shapes who can use the crossing
sections.text: The published payment page describes free-flow collection through HGS and says the tollbooths do not take cash or credit cards. Its vehicle-class text includes eligible two-axle vehicles and a distinct motorcycle tariff, so a generic description limited to cars alone would be incomplete. The availability of online payment is not permission for every vehicle to enter. This review inspected the public description without querying a plate, opening an account or making a payment. It does not reproduce a tariff as travel advice or claim that a payment interface was tested successfully.

sections.heading: What would improve this account
sections.text: Editorial evidence test: connect the concession's published obligations to dated operating records with clear denominators. Separate traffic counts, closure hours, incident severity, payment disputes and public financial transfers rather than merging them into a single performance score. An auditable model of time and emissions savings would need an explicit alternative scenario and a reporting period matching the traffic data. The present sources support a bounded operating-project account and a description of governance. They do not authorize calling every claimed benefit independently verified or substituting this road crossing's evidence for the neighbouring railway.

next_artifacts: Underlying 2025 performance definitions, model assumptions and comparable traffic series.
Dated closures, incidents and response-time records with denominators.
Actual concession-related public financial reporting distinct from original investment and modeled benefits.

records.title: Istanbul: municipal services across a cross-strait city
records.answer: Istanbul's service account combines water, housing access, childcare, transport accessibility and building-risk screening. Municipal provision, national housing programmes and separate transport operators must retain their own responsibilities and evidence limits.
records.scope: One Istanbul metropolitan municipal territory. Districts, service facilities and individual water, childcare or screening examples are not additional counted identities; the wider regional catchment and Marmaray's Gebze end are not absorbed into this place.
records.stage: The inspected record includes a reported water-tunnel opening, national rental-housing applications and published municipal service arrangements. Indexed source access is explicit; design capacity, application eligibility and structural screening are not universal delivered outcomes.

identity_decision.rationale: Count Istanbul's metropolitan municipal territory once and explain its services without turning districts or illustrative facilities into extra places. Keep national TOKİ housing, municipal service providers and the interprovincial Marmaray corridor distinct; no national or historical acquisition docket is reused.

timeline.event: The later municipal water-tunnel account reports completion of excavation.
The water account reports pipe installation completed by the end of the year.
The same account dates the start of testing to April.
Publication of the municipal water-tunnel opening report; this is not assigned as the ceremony date.
TOKİ's later account dates the start of rental-housing applications.
Applications closed, derived from the September 26 report's explicit statement that closure was the previous day.

sections.heading: Water commissioning is not a delivered-volume series
sections.text: The municipal September 11 account reports the opening of the Kâğıthane–Bahçelievler–Sefaköy drinking-water tunnel. It describes 20,630 metres of tunnel, eleven shafts and capacity to carry 1.5 million cubic metres daily. Its construction sequence places excavation completion in 2024, pipe installation by the end of 2025 and testing from April 2026. Those milestones are more informative than treating the publication date as the date of every event. Design throughput is not measured household delivery. Direct retrieval timed out; this account uses the official indexed text and does not claim verification of the unavailable water-balance PDF.

sections.heading: A national housing programme within the city
sections.text: TOKİ's September 26 report says rental-housing applications had closed the previous day after opening September 14. It identifies a first group of 1,071 homes and describes screening, an October lottery and later handover. These are application-stage and forecast allocation steps, not evidence that the homes were occupied. The agency is national; including its programme in an Istanbul place account does not turn it into municipal ownership. Published eligibility categories also do not measure how far the programme meets total housing need. A later tenancy and occupancy record would answer a different question from application closure.

sections.heading: Childcare has admission and calendar boundaries
sections.text: Yuvamız İstanbul's indexed FAQ describes full-day provision rather than hourly or half-day use, with an eleven-month service year and an August break. Admission is ranked using declared information subject to document checks; free and paid categories are distinct. The same FAQ describes specialist assessment for children with additional needs and specific provision at named centres, not identical support everywhere. These details matter to an account of access: a service can exist without a place being available to every household. No family application or live availability query was submitted, and the full live page could not be retrieved.

sections.heading: Accessibility belongs to a named operator and route
sections.text: Metro İstanbul's indexed accessibility description lists lifts, escalators, ramps, guidance and tactile surfaces as parts of its access provision. It explains an approach to helping passengers reach stations and vehicles, rather than providing a live inventory of working equipment. This operator's network must remain distinct from Marmaray. Its description cannot certify another operator's platforms or guarantee an uninterrupted step-free trip on a specific date. A useful city-level comparison would retain each operator and station identity and report interruptions consistently. The present account inspected the published description, not equipment, staff assistance or a passenger journey.

sections.heading: Screening identifies questions; it does not certify safety
sections.text: The municipality's building-screening FAQ describes address-based risk ranking using information collected within buildings. It sets limits by age, use and structural type, including the applicable reinforced-concrete and masonry height categories. The separate application notice explains that detailed assessment under the specified statutory or building-code framework remains necessary for definitive risk evaluation and associated entitlements. Rapid screening is not a building-safety certificate. Both records were available as official indexed text after direct retrieval timed out. No address was submitted, private result obtained, structural diagnosis made or legal eligibility decision issued in this editorial review.

sections.heading: What would improve this account
sections.text: Editorial evidence test: make service access measurable without confusing institutional roles. Seek water delivery and interruption records, occupied rental homes by allocation cohort, childcare waiting times and attendance, station equipment availability, and documented follow-through after risk screening. Preserve each denominator and geographical boundary. Regional source water does not expand the municipality; a railway continuing into another province does not move that province into Istanbul. The three dossiers provide linked but separate identities. Their next evidence should test the experience of residents and users, while retaining the difference between announced provision, eligibility, commissioning and actual recurring outcomes.

next_artifacts: Dated delivered-water volumes and interruptions, with source and municipal service boundaries.
Confirmed housing occupancy and childcare admission/waiting-time outcomes by cohort.
Operator-specific accessibility availability and documented screening follow-through, without private resident data.
